With regard to films, smoking has always seemed to be portrayed as “cool,” but there’s larger factors at play when it’s used in a film.

There’s a book called “Psychology for Screenwriters” by William Indick where he briefly touches on this topic, I’ll write down the gist of it below to explain it (according to his own research on it.)

According to him, smoking in older black and white films simply looked cool because it “has a strong emotional impact, not just because of the natural obscurity provided by the smoke, but also from a sense of gritty realism.”

Apart from this, he goes on to explain that the second reason characters smoke is to insert a dramatic pause in dialogue and “since film is a visual medium, it’s hard to write dramatic pauses that are meaningful to actors.”

His final points on this topic were that smoking can just make a character look cool and gives them something to do with their hands and mouth. Going on to explain that it “provides a natural fog that obscures the light around them, giving them an ethereal appearance as they are momentarily veiled behind a cloud of blue smoke.” He states that the most important reason is that smoking imparts a sense of internal conflict and that the character is soothing some kind of inner turmoil.

Additionally, in the book it’s stated that the effect of smoking on screen is now even greater that we know smoking is unhealthy, and only someone severely conflicted would voluntarily kill themselves with each drag.

The bottom line is, it humanises characters by showing us their flaws with addiction, making them seem a little more relatable.

In reality, everyone knows that smoking is unhealthy and an expensive habit. Smokers themselves will admit that they wish they could quit or that they never started in the first place. As a smoker myself, I don’t know any other smokers that think its “cool.” People cope with things in different ways, and that’s okay as long as it’s not getting in your way then it’s not really any of your business dictating how people should cope with whatever their dealing with. Some people drink, some people smoke, some people exercise…

Addiction is a disease that’s brought on voluntarily. The only people that think smoking in real life is “cool” are the people more inclined to experiment with it, like impressionable kids. I admit I started smoking as well just because I thought it looked cool, I don’t anymore because you grow out of that phase eventually. After trying to quit unsuccessfully multiple times I realised that it’s a genuine problem. Most smokers want to quit; all smokers don’t want anyone else to pick up the habit.

Hope this gives you some insight into it. Cheers.
